title: provider-auth -01 §7: say that presenting a client certificate the target does not trust denies you the other mechanisms
design:
FROM bead mimid-75nk.14, which fixed mimid's half. The draft's half is a
sentence that is not there.

WHAT -00 §7 SAYS. A provider "MAY present a client certificate", and
nothing about the consequence of presenting one the target does not
trust. That reads as a free choice. It is not: it is a choice that can
take a working peer offline.

WHAT HAPPENS, verified against Haven's public hub on 2026-11-22 and
reproduced offline in crates/mimid-server/tests/peer_client_tls.rs:

  signature only                -> 200, handle resolved
  signature + our client cert   -> tlsv1 alert unknown ca, no HTTP at all

Every link is defensible. The target asks for a client certificate but
does not require one, which is the correct configuration for a provider
that wants PKIX from the peers that have it and signatures from the rest.
Offered a certificate from a CA it does not know, it rejects it at the
TLS layer. The handshake then dies before any HTTP request is sent, so
the RFC 9421 signature -- the mechanism that would have authenticated the
request -- is never seen. The source provider cannot tell this apart from
the target being down.

So presenting an untrusted client certificate is strictly WORSE than
presenting none, and the draft should say so, because an implementer
reading §7's "MAY" will not guess it.

PROPOSED TEXT, for §7, to be shortened by whoever edits it:

  A source provider SHOULD NOT present a client certificate to a target
  provider unless it has reason to believe the target trusts the issuer.
  A target that requests but does not require client certificates will
  reject an untrusted certificate during the TLS handshake, which denies
  the source provider the other authentication mechanisms in this
  document: the handshake fails before any HTTP request is sent, so a
  request signature (Section 5) is never evaluated. A source provider
  therefore SHOULD make the decision per target provider rather than
  globally, and a target provider MAY advertise the issuers it trusts.

The last clause is the weakest and may be worth dropping: there is no
mechanism here for advertising issuers, and TLS's own
certificate_authorities extension exists but Haven does not send it
(verified: exactly one CertificateRequest in the handshake, no CA list).
Raising the question may be better than answering it.

WORTH ASKING THE WG rather than only asserting: whether a target that
requests client certificates SHOULD send certificate_authorities, since
that would let a source decide correctly without configuration. That is
the real fix and it belongs in the draft rather than in each
implementation's configuration file.

Posting needs Mark's OK, like any upstream post. This blocks
mimid-75nk.11 (posting -01), so the draft does not go out without it.
